cells.quote: VEP modeling projects that data centers could account for more than 90% of the Commonwealth's electricity-demand growth over the next two decades.

Continuing to implement robust protections and cost allocation practices will be essential to protect residential, small businesses, and other ratepayers from the infrastructure costs caused by data centers.
cells.note: States a principle

cells.quote: The SCC has created a separate large load rate class for Dominion Energy Virginia and related service terms for qualifying large load customers
cells.note: Effective 2027 per the plan

cells.quote: qualifying large load customers, including a 14-year contract term, minimum demand charges, collateral requirements, and exit-fee provisions, effective January 1, 2027.
the SCC directed revisions to Dominion's proposed large load connection queue
cells.note: Ongoing proceeding

cells.quote: The Distributed Flexibility Scenario assumes all data centers provide the equivalent of a 10% reduction in peak demand.
cells.note: Modeled scenario, not an adopted rule

cells.quote: this could include promoting large load offtake models, large multi-unit orderbooks, ring-fenced subsidiary investment
cells.note: Nuclear financing structures

cells.quote: 30 of the 32 GW of projected load growth by 2030 is associated with large load data center construction in the PJM region
cells.note: PJM forecast cited by the plan

cells.quote: New load from data centers will enter the PJM system rapidly, and PJM can create new mechanisms to help accelerate the deployment of new resources. However, to the extent that new load enters the system before matching new generation, PJM must also ensure the new load enters the system flexibly to protect ratepayer costs and grid reliability.
cells.note: Expectation placed on PJM, not a state rule

cells.quote: The ongoing Large Load Critical Issue Fast Path charge at PJM is the most direct process addressing the issue, but load forecasting, interconnection processes, and market structure must also broadly be considered.
cells.note: Points to a PJM process

cells.quote: PacifiCorp has had interruptible contracts with large load customers for many years. These contracts are a key aspect of the retail service provided to the associated customers
cells.note: Existing interruptible contracts

cells.quote: driven by lower projected demand from new large customers who are expected to bring their own resources, thus lowering the commercial forecast.
cells.note: Planning assumption in the load forecast

cells.quote:
The Company has seen unprecedent levels of growth in both the size and number of requests for delivery points in the last several years, including the significant increase in volume and increased size from large-
load customers. As of February 2026, approximately 25,000 megawatts of large-load delivery point requests
cells.note: Requests received as of Feb 2026

cells.quote: To ensure data centers and other high load customers continue to pay their fair share and to mitigate against stranded costs, the Company proposed, and the SCC approved, a robust package of cost allocation, rate design, and Terms and Conditions changes
cells.note: SCC-approved package per the utility

cells.quote: To ensure data centers and other high load customers continue to pay their fair share and to mitigate against stranded costs, the Company proposed, and the SCC approved, a robust package of cost allocation, rate design, and Terms and Conditions changes in the Company's biennial review proceeding, Case No. PUR-2025-00058. Notably, the Company's proposals included the creation of a new customer class for its most energy-intensive customers.
cells.note: New customer class (GS-5)

cells.quote: Execution of this agreement protects the Company, as discussed below, allows the distribution team to add the data center project to our queue, and begins the engineering study and design processes that are prerequisites to connect to the grid. At signing, a $250,000 deposit is required
cells.note: Deposit at ELOA signing

cells.quote: The connection process begins when a data center submits a request for service to Dominion Energy's distribution team. The request must include a site plan or building layout, requested energization date, the capacity being requested including a ramp schedule, and meter voltage
cells.note: Request, ELOA, queue

cells.quote: the Company is evaluating potential financing approaches and commercial structures, including arrangements with third parties and large-load customers, that may improve project economics
cells.note: SMR financing with large-load customers

cells.quote: As of July 31, 2025, the Company has 16,913 MW of requested capacity under firm contracts through executed ESAs or CLOAs. The Company is currently studying an additional 30,132 MW of data center capacity at the ELOA stage.
cells.note: As of July 2025

cells.quote: The Company uses a three-contract structure with large load customers that bind customers to increasing financial commitments as projects progress.
cells.note: ESA, CLOA, ELOA

cells.quote: interconnect data center customers
cells.note: Transmission action item only

cells.quote: Dominion Energy continues to explore opportunities for and interest in demand response programs with its largest customers. To date, data centers have been hesitant to participate in demand response
cells.note: Exploring; customers hesitant
